QML.2605.31248: |**2026-05-29**|**Trainable Quantum Spectral Models for Partial Differential Equations**|Achim Streit|quant-ph|[2605.31248](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.31248)||This work studies trainable quantum spectral models (QSMs) for solving linear partial differential equations (PDEs). QML.2605.31006: |**2026-05-29**|**Quantum State Preparation via Neural Network Encoding in Quantum Machine Learning**|Andre Luckow|quant-ph|[2605.31006](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.31006)||A central challenge in quantum machine learning is the state preparation bottleneck that describes the prohibitive computational cost of loading high-dimensional classical data into a quantum state. QML.2605.30724: |**2026-05-29**|**Research progress on quantum neural networks and quantum machine learning**|Xiangdong Zhang|quant-ph|[2605.30724](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30724)|47 pages, 8 figures|Machine learning holds fundamental computational significance due to the increasing demand for efficient solutions to complex tasks in data analysis, pattern recognition, and optimization, which are essential for addressing the multifaceted challenges of modern society. QML.2605.30572: |**2026-05-28**|**Mitigating Noise-Induced Barren Plateaus Using a Non-Unitary Ansatz: Application to Molecular Electronic Transport**|Michael Kolodrubetz|quant-ph|[2605.30572](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30572)|29 pages, 17 figures|Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) offer a promising route toward simulating many-body quantum systems on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. QML.2605.29557: |**2026-05-28**|**Quantum Subliminal Learning**|Yu-Qin Chen|quant-ph|[2605.29557](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29557)|4.5 pages, 3 figures, with supplemental materials|Machine learning models can inherit hidden behavioral traits through innocuous public interfaces, a phenomenon known as subliminal learning. QML.2605.28723: |**2026-05-27**|**Variational Quantum Models for Knowledge Graph Embeddings on NISQ Devices**|Gustavo Martín Bosyk|quant-ph|[2605.28723](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28723)||Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) combine quantum circuits with classical optimization to tackle problems that may benefit from the capabilities of near-term quantum hardware.
